assertion_audit.fails_if: The named real-home pointer exists before setup; this guards fixture targeting, not the landing regression.
The test creates or leaves that named pointer in the real home; independent filesystem check, but not a census of every real-home write.
The reviewed commit is already on the remote primary branch before the call; this is a meaningful negative precondition.
Restoring the old pointer-race exception returns CLI exit 1; base and mutant logs demonstrate this failure.
The caller reports success without merging/pushing the reviewed commit; actual Git ancestry is independent of the supplied head argument, although surviving file content is not checked.
Retirement is omitted and the original pointer survives after success.
The pending record is written but clear_pending is removed; it also passes if the pending writer is removed, so it cannot establish pending-record durability.
Restoring the old exception on the newer pointer makes the CLI fail; shown in both red logs.
Landing is skipped while success is returned, leaving the reviewed commit absent from the remote branch.
The newer attempt is removed or its attempt number changes away from independently specified 4; it does not fail when pending_landing_repair is incorrectly added.

assertion_independence: No added assertion is a self-equality against a supplied value: ancestry reads Git state and attempt 4 is independently specified; gaps are missing state/content assertions, not tautologies.

findings.text: blocking: when _retire_a_raced_pointer refuses a newer attempt, _keep_pointer_for_pending_landing marks that newer live pointer pending_landing_repair; the caller then succeeds and clears the pending file at crew_run_commands.py:4043, leaving a newer attempt whose next complete takes the repair-only branch at lines 3626-3641 and cannot find a record to finish; leave the newer attempt's repair state untouched and assert that state in the second test.
